title: Bee Ulmo Wins Platinum Award for Best Quality at 2023 London Honey Awards
htmlContent:
The pristine wilderness of Chilean Patagonia is where Bee Ulmo honey brand comes from, and it just received the prestigious Platinum Award for Best Quality at the 2023 London Honey Awards. Just a few months after obtaining the same distinction at the Paris International Honey Awards. Bee Ulmo's commitment to excellence with its premium APF 200+ Ulmo Honey, which is praised for its purity and potent health benefits, is highlighted by this recognition. Bee Ulmo's honey is made by bees who gather nectar exclusively from the Ulmo tree, a species native to Chilean Patagonia, and is inspected rigorously to ensure authenticity. The Catholic University of Chile tests and certifies each batch to confirm its APF (Active Patagonia Factor) level, which indicates antibacterial potency.
"Our honey meets APF certifications ranging from 100+ to 200+," says Bee Ulmo co-founders Ruben Lhasa and Romina Raffo. "The higher the APF, the stronger the antibacterial properties."
The pristine environment of Chilean Patagonia's largely untouched landscape has earned it a worldwide reputation. Bee Ulmo utilizes its purity by harvesting raw Ulmo Honey in small, carefully managed batches to keep it in its natural state. Bee Ulmo's Ulmo Honey is different from other commercially processed honeys in that it remains unheated and unfiltered, with a creamy texture and a rich profile of vitamins, minerals, and enzymes.
“Our honey is never mixed or artificially enhanced, ensuring the maximum health benefits of its antibacterial, anti-inflammatory, and immune-boosting properties,” Lhasa and Raffo explain.
Health professionals express their appreciation for high-APF honey's support of immune health and overall wellness, which includes benefits for kidney and urinary tract health, circulation, and joint health. As functional foods become more popular, Bee Ulmo is becoming a natural supplement for health-conscious consumers worldwide. In addition to producing top-notch honey, Bee Ulmo is committed to sustaining practices and fostering economic prosperity in Chilean Patagonia. “We aim to foster sustainable jobs in a growing Ulmo Honey industry that can positively impact thousands of lives,” Lhasa notes. Bee Ulmo donates 1% of its sales or 10% of its profits each year to environmental initiatives to reinforce the brand's commitment to global stewardship. In the United States, China, the Middle East, the Netherlands, and Spain, Bee Ulmo is now offering the world the exceptional taste and benefits of Ulmo Honey. Visit beeulmo.com for more details or to make a purchase.
